# Literature Radar

A living overview of new research from selected journals, collected automatically from PubMed.

~~~{r}
source("../R/site.R")
site <- load_literature_site_data("..")
enabled_journals <- Filter(function(x) isTRUE(x$enabled), site$journals)
~~~

~~~{r, results='asis'}
stats <- list(
  c(label = "Papers indexed", value = format(site$paper_count, big.mark = ",")),
  c(label = "Journals monitored", value = as.character(length(enabled_journals))),
  c(label = "Retrieval reports", value = as.character(site$report_count)),
  c(label = "AI summaries", value = as.character(site$summary_count))
)
cat('<div class="stats-grid">')
for (stat in stats) {
  cat(sprintf(
    '<div class="stat-card"><div class="stat-value">%s</div><div class="stat-label">%s</div></div>',
    site_html_escape(stat[["value"]]), site_html_escape(stat[["label"]])
  ))
}
cat('</div>')
if (nzchar(site$latest_update)) {
  cat(sprintf('<p class="last-updated">Latest retrieval report: %s</p>', site_html_escape(site$latest_update)))
}
~~~

## Journal monitoring

The weekly retrieval process prioritizes journals with the oldest successful retrieval history. Three journals are normally processed per run; each journal has its own retrieval cursor.

~~~{r, results='asis'}
cat('<div class="journal-grid">')
for (journal in enabled_journals) {
  latest <- journal$latest_report
  if (is.null(latest)) {
    report_line <- "No retrieval report yet"
  } else {
    report_line <- paste0(
      "Latest window: ", latest$start_date, " to ", latest$end_date,
      " · ", latest$new_count, " new papers"
    )
  }
  anchor <- gsub("[^a-z0-9-]", "-", tolower(journal$id))
  cat(sprintf(
    '<article class="journal-tile"><h3>%s</h3><p>%s</p><a href="papers.html#%s">Browse papers</a></article>',
    site_html_escape(journal$name), site_html_escape(report_line), site_html_escape(anchor)
  ))
}
cat('</div>')
~~~

## About the data

- Records are retrieved from **PubMed** using PubMed Create Date, not publication date.
- Retrieval reports are immutable; overlapping windows prevent missed records without repeating previously indexed PMIDs.
- AI-generated summaries are available only for papers included in an Ollama summarization run. Other papers are shown with their original abstracts.

Browse the [paper collection](papers.qmd) or inspect the [source repository](https://github.com/gabnasello/literature-radar).
